paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: strong faith is built for carrying, not for winning. Paul says we who are strong ought to "bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves" (Romans 15:1). And he says it as WE, so he's not pointing at anybody from a safe distance. The strong are strong so somebody else has a hand to hold.

So why would anyone live like that? Because Christ did. "Even Christ did not please Himself" (Romans 15:3), and then Paul says to accept one another "just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God" (Romans 15:7). Think about that. You didn't earn your seat at the table, friend, and I sure didn't earn mine, a 25 cent stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer. When you know how you were accepted, you've got no good reason to hold the door half shut for the next person.

Paul keeps going back to Scripture and to hope, and that's the engine behind all of it. What was written before us was written "for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope" (Romans 15:4). Four verses in a row show the Gentiles praising God alongside His people, so this welcome was never an accident. So the next time someone in your life is hard to bear with, remember where your patience comes from: "the God of hope" who can fill you "with all joy and peace" so you "overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit" (Romans 15:13).
